surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EPS was $1.04, well below the preview’s $1.18–$1.20 consensus range. The preview expected an EPS decline from the prior year, but not a miss of this size versus estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 adjusted diluted EPS was $1.04, down from $1.27 in Q3 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Treat $1.18–$1.20 as the number that matters” for adjusted EPS.

surprises.description: Quadvest is expected to dilute 2026 adjusted EPS by only about 6% versus the stand-alone midpoint, below the previously communicated 10%–20% range. The October 1 closing, later than the originally assumed mid-2026 date, explains the smaller first-year impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Quadvest acquisition's 2026 dilution is only ~6% versus the stand-alone midpoint, well below the previously communicated 10%-20% range,” because it closed October 1 rather than at the originally assumed mid-2026 date.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has previously framed stepped-up fair-value depreciation as 10–20% of standalone plan dilution until 2028 rates.”

surprises.description: Management said Quadvest dilution in 2027 will trend toward the high end of the 10%–20% range, reflecting a full year of operations and stepped-up depreciation. That gives a more adverse 2027 dilution outlook than the preview’s general 10%–20% framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects 2027 dilution to trend toward the higher end of the 10%-20% range,” driven by a full year of Quadvest operations and stepped-up depreciation.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had framed dilution as “10–20% of standalone plan dilution until 2028 rates” and flagged the need for 2027 framing.

surprises.description: The company reduced 2026 company-funded CapEx to about $465 million from $483 million, but attributed the reduction to more developer-funded Texas capital rather than a cut to the investment plan. That eases the preview’s concern that underspending could signal slower rate-base growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2026 company-funded CapEx was lowered to ~$465 million from $483 million due to higher developer-funded capital in Texas,” while the five-year consolidated budget remains $2.7 billion and Texas CapEx remains $766 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted $206.9 million deployed against the $483 million budget and warned, “Under-spend reads as rate base growth slipping.”

surprises.description: Management stated that the $2.7 billion capital plan plus Quadvest is expected to deliver a 13% rate-base CAGR and that long-term EPS CAGR is targeted at or above the top of the 6%–8% range. That is a stronger stated growth target than the preview’s 6%–8% framing and its concern that Street estimates implied a 2027 decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The $2.7 billion capital plan plus Quadvest is expected to drive a 13% rate base CAGR” and long-term EPS CAGR is “targeted at or above the top of the 6%-8% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referred to management’s “6–8% CAGR target” and noted the Street’s FY2027 EPS estimate was “around $2.84,” below the FY2026 guide.
